description: Azure Table and Blob storage-aware state manager support for Egil.Orleans.Messaging.
releaseNotes:
New Features:
- configure lifecycle hooks through callbacks
  Configure hooks with a callback that receives a library-owned configuration object. Consumers can assign handlers without constructing options, and async registration accepts the same callback shape.
  Copy validated handlers before installing them so retained configuration objects cannot change active or future operations. Failed configuration leaves existing hooks intact. Update examples and migration guidance for custom managers, and verify callback execution, snapshot isolation, and activation behavior.
- add state manager lifecycle hooks
  Add synchronous and awaited asynchronous read, write, clear, and common callbacks for confirmed storage outcomes. Preserve durable state and report callback failures without retrying storage; capture configuration per operation and reject nested storage operations.
  Await initial read handlers for injected, constructor-registered, and asynchronously registered managers. Add ConfigureHooks and InitializeAsync to IStateManager<T>, with migration guidance for custom implementations. This follows the reviewed issue #257 plan and includes activation, recovery, cancellation, and reconfiguration coverage.
Bug Fixes:
- scope hook reentrancy guards to each async flow
  Keep nested storage operations rejected throughout each lifecycle handler, including after awaits and when another dispatch completes. Track handler depth per async execution flow so independent reentrant operations are not incorrectly rejected.
  Address both PR #258 guard review findings with deterministic overlapping-dispatch and independent-flow regressions, plus focused asynchronous write and clear handler coverage.
- preserve wrapped default-manager conflicts
  The default state manager now recognizes wrapped concurrency conflicts during writes and clears. Recovery refreshes local state and its ETag, then rethrows the original exception even when the stored value matches or the record is absent.
  Aggregates containing only conflicts follow the same rule. Mixed aggregates retain unknown-outcome recovery so an uncertain earlier attempt is not mistaken for a definite rejection.
- preserve recovery-free Azure rejections
  Missing containers and tables and non-ETag precondition failures continue to restore the previous state and rethrow without reading storage. Specific Azure error codes now take precedence over broad conflict status codes, while ambiguous failures retain read-back recovery.
  Clarify the recovery matrix and Azure guidance so concurrency conflicts always refresh state and rethrow, even when values match.
- re-read after Azure ETag conflict via new Conflict classification
  Split optimistic-concurrency rejections out of `StorageFailureKind.DidNotPersist`
  into a new `Conflict` value. `StateManagerBase` now runs read-back recovery on
  `Conflict`, adopts the persisted state and refreshed ETag, and always rethrows —
  a coincidental value match must not hide a concurrent write. `AzureStorage-
  StateManager<T>` classifies `InconsistentStateException`, HTTP 412/409/404, and
  ETag/existence error codes (`ConditionNotMet`, `UpdateConditionNotSatisfied`,
  `BlobAlreadyExists`/`BlobNotFound`, `EntityAlreadyExists`/`EntityNotFound`,
  `ResourceAlreadyExists`/`ResourceNotFound`) as `Conflict`; other
  client-side rejections stay `DidNotPersist`. Aggregate precedence is
  `UnknownOutcome` > `Conflict` > `DidNotPersist`. Fixes grains that stayed
  stuck retransmitting a stale ETag after a 5xx-then-412 retry sequence.
  Closes #261
